mainTopic: Proving רב חסדא's reading of רב about a קטנה and a חרשת from a ברייתא that follows the רבנן, and the start of a new משנה about two orphaned minors
overview: This amud continues the discussion of two orphaned sisters, a קטנה and a חרשת, married to two brothers. The גמרא shows that only רב חסדא's reading of רב works: the חרשת is partly married, and the קטנה's marriage is a 'maybe'. רב ששת supports this reading with a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, a חרשת who falls to her sister's husband is released by relations followed by a גט, and that only makes sense under רב חסדא's reading. The גמרא pushes back that the ברייתא might follow רבי נחמיה, who holds that a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה exempts from חליצה. But the last clause of the ברייתא requires a קטנה to do חליצה, which fits only the רבנן, so the proof stands. רב אשי tries to bring another proof from the first clause, but the גמרא pushes it off. The amud ends by opening a new משנה about a man married to two orphaned minor girls.

steps.title: Either way, she should be allowed to stay with him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues its challenge against a reading of רב's ruling: if the חרשת's marriage to him was only a maybe, he should be able to keep her as his wife (rather than divorce her) no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her stay with him, whichever way you look at it. If she was truly married, she is truly married. If she was not married at all, she is simply an unrelated woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of attacking one way of understanding רב's ruling. It says this understanding leads to a strange result: there should be no reason to make the חרשת leave her husband when her sister falls to him for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a ממה נפשך, meaning it covers both possibilities. If her marriage to him was real, she is fully his wife, and her sister's זיקה cannot take hold on her. If it was never a marriage, she is just an unrelated woman, and the קטנה's חליצה does not forbid her to him. So treating her as a 'maybe' cannot forbid her.

keyTerms.meaning: Let her stay with him (as his wife)
Whichever way you look at it; covering both sides of a doubt
Acquired, meaning truly married
Merely an unrelated woman, with no family tie that would forbid her

steps.confusionAlert: Here נכרית does not mean a non-Jewish woman. It means a woman who is a stranger to this family, with no real marriage tie that would make her forbidden.

phrases.english: Let her stay with him, whichever way you look at it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קְנוּיָה הִיא — הָא קְנוּיָה הִיא,
phrases.english: If she is acquired, then she is acquired;
and if she is not acquired,
then she is merely an unrelated woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an earlier challenge against another reading of רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב's ruling that treats this widow's marriage as only possibly valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A marriage that is only a maybe cannot forbid her. On both sides of the doubt she is permitted to the brother, so the ruling that she must leave him makes no sense.

steps.title: The same question seems to work against the minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects someone to push back: the same 'either way' question could be asked about the קטנה in רב חסדא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: why should the minor wait until she grows up and does חליצה? Let her stay with him. If she was truly married, she is truly married. If she was not married at all, she is simply an unrelated woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible counter-challenge. It turns the same 'either way' argument against רב חסדא's reading, where the קטנה's marriage is the uncertain one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב חסדא's reading, the קטנה's marriage is the doubtful one, and she has to wait until she is an adult to do חליצה. The challenger says the same logic should apply to her: either she was married or she was a stranger, so either way the brother could keep her. This step only sets up the question; the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; brings up a challenge someone might raise
A girl who is not yet an adult
She must wait until she grows up
She will do חליצה, the ceremony that releases her from יבום

phrases.english: And if you will say: why should the minor wait
until she grows up and does חליצה?
Let her stay with him!

phrases.aramaic: אִי קְנוּיָה הִיא — הָא קְנוּיָה הִיא,
phrases.english: If she is acquired, then she is acquired;
if she is not acquired,
she is merely an unrelated woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, קְטַנָּה אַמַּאי תַּמְתִּין עַד שֶׁתַּגְדִּיל וְתַחְלוֹץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 1's 'either way' argument against רב חסדא's own reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading, which treats the קטנה's marriage as uncertain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a doubtful marriage cannot forbid a woman, then the קטנה should not have to wait for חליצה. She should simply stay with him.

steps.title: Otherwise, how would the deaf woman ever be released?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the קטנה cannot just stay with him, because then there would be no way at all to release the חרשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how would the deaf woman ever get out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 2. Letting the קטנה stay would leave the חרשת stuck, with no way to be released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרשת cannot do חליצה. If the brother kept the קטנה, the חרשת would be stuck in a bad spot, because the קטנה might count as his יבמה and the חרשת is her sister. Only רב חסדא's setup gives both women a way out: the חרשת leaves with a גט, and the קטנה waits and does חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; points out what would go wrong
A deaf woman who cannot speak, who in halacha cannot do חליצה
By what means will she go out, meaning be released

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's ruling was built so that both sisters end up free, and that only רב חסדא's reading gets that result.

phrases.english: If so, by what means would the deaf-mute go out?
phrases.notes: She cannot do חליצה, so without the plan in רב's ruling she would have no way to be released.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical need: the ruling has to give both women a way to be released.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רב חסדא's reading, the קטנה could simply stay with the brother whichever way you look at it.
steps.terutzMaskana: She must wait and do חליצה. Otherwise the חרשת, who cannot do חליצה, would have no way to be released.

steps.title: רב ששת agrees with רב חסדא's reading
steps.stepSummary: רב שׁשׁת says that רב חסדא's way of explaining רב is also what makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שׁשׁת said: It also makes sense, just as רב חסדא explained according to רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שׁשׁת comes out in support of רב חסדא's reading of רב. This line sets up the proof he is about to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא used logic. Now רב שׁשׁת says he can back up רב חסדא's reading with a source, and the next step brings that source.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense; agreeing with a view
Explains, meaning sets out the correct reading
According to רב

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָכִי נָמֵי מִיסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: So too it makes sense,

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְקָא מְתָרֵץ רַב חִסְדָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְרַב,
phrases.english: just as Rav Ḥisda explained according to Rav,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָכִי נָמֵי מִיסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא's support for the conclusion of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא's reading of רב is the reasonable one.

steps.title: A ברייתא with the same case and the same rulings
steps.stepSummary: רב שׁשׁת brings a ברייתא about two orphaned sisters, a קטנה and a חרשת: the חרשת leaves with a גט, and the קטנה waits until she grows up and does חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Two brothers were married to two orphaned sisters, one a minor and one a deaf-mute. If the minor's husband died, the deaf-mute goes out with a גט, and the minor waits until she grows up and does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for רב שׁשׁת's statement. The ברייתא gives the same rulings that רב חסדא's reading gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first case gives the same rulings as רב: the חרשת leaves with a גט, and the קטנה waits for חליצה. On its own it does not yet prove which reading of רב is right. The actual proof comes from the ברייתא's next case, where the חרשת's husband dies (steps 6-8).

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans; girls without a father to marry them off
She goes out with a bill of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of two orphaned sisters, a קטנה and a חרשת, where the קטנה's husband died: the חרשת leaves with a גט, and the קטנה waits until she is an adult and does חליצה. The proof for רב חסדא comes from the next case in the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Two brothers married
two orphaned sisters, a minor and a deaf-mute;
the husband of the minor died,
phrases.notes: So the minor now falls to the other brother for יבום, and he is the deaf-mute's husband.

phrases.english: the deaf-mute goes out with a bill of divorce,
and the minor waits until she grows up, and does חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁנֵי אַחִין נְשׂוּאִין שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת יְתוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs רב שׁשׁת's statement in step 4.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two orphaned sisters, a קטנה and a חרשת. Its second case, where relations with the חרשת followed by a גט release her, is the part that supports רב חסדא (steps 6-8).

steps.title: The second case in the ברייתא: the deaf-mute's husband dies
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the חרשת's husband dies, the קטנה leaves with a גט and the חרשת is forbidden forever. But if he did have relations with the חרשת, he gives her a גט and she is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the deaf-mute's husband died, the minor leaves with a גט, and the deaf-mute is forbidden forever. And if he had relations with the deaf-mute, he gives her a גט, and she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is still quoting the same ברייתא from step 5. Now it gives the opposite case, where the חרשת's husband is the one who died. This line is the setup for the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surviving brother is married to the קטנה, and now her sister, the חרשת, falls to him for יבום. He sends away his own wife, the קטנה, with a גט. He cannot do יבום with the חרשת because she is his wife's sister, and she cannot do חליצה, so she is stuck forever. The key detail is the last line: if he went ahead and had relations with her anyway, a גט is enough to release her.

keyTerms.meaning: her husband died
forbidden forever (she can never remarry)
had relations with
and she is permitted (free to remarry)

phrases.english: If the husband of the deaf-mute died —
the minor leaves with a גט,
phrases.notes: The minor is the surviving brother's own wife. He has to divorce her because her sister now falls to him for יבום.

phrases.english: and the deaf-mute is forbidden forever.
And if he had relations with the deaf-mute —
he gives her a גט, and she is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 5 with its second case.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's reading of רב: the חרשת is partly acquired and the קטנה is a 'maybe'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about two orphaned sisters, a קטנה and a חרשת, married to two brothers.

steps.title: Why the ruling works under רב חסדא's reading
steps.stepSummary: If the חרשת is partly acquired and the קטנה is a 'maybe', then his relations with the חרשת release her either way. If the קטנה was truly his wife, the חרשת is exempt as his wife's sister. If the קטנה was not his wife, his יבום was perfectly valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say the deaf-mute is partly acquired and the minor is maybe acquired, maybe not. That is why, when he has relations with the deaf-mute, he gives her a גט and she is permitted. You can say 'either way': if the minor is acquired, the deaf-mute is out because she is his wife's sister. If the minor is not acquired, he did a proper יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now explains how the ברייתא proves רב חסדא right. Under רב חסדא's reading, the ruling that the חרשת is released makes sense no matter how you look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב חסדא, the קטנה's marriage is a pure 'maybe'. So there are only two options, and both lead to the חרשת being free. Either she was totally exempt from יבום as his wife's sister, or his relations with her were a valid יבום, which a גט can then end.

keyTerms.meaning: acquired, but with something left over (partly married)
maybe acquired, maybe not (a doubtful marriage)
either way; whichever side you take
a wife's sister (forbidden, and exempt from יבום)
does יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two phrases. קנויה ומשויירת means a real but partial marriage. קנויה ואינה קנויה means we simply do not know whether there is a marriage at all.

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say
the deaf-mute is acquired but not completely,
and the minor is maybe acquired, maybe not acquired —
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא's way of reading רב.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי דְּכִי בָּא עַל הַחֵרֶשֶׁת
phrases.english: that is why, when he has relations with the deaf-mute,
he gives her a גט and she is permitted,
because you can say 'either way':
if the minor is acquired —
then the deaf-mute is out because she is his wife's sister,
if the minor is not acquired —
he did a proper יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the ruling in step 6 fits רב חסדא's reading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that relations with the חרשת followed by a גט release her.

steps.title: Why the other reading cannot explain the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: If you flip it, so the חרשת is a 'maybe' and the קטנה is partly acquired, then his relations with the חרשת would be a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה. A flawed act does not exempt her, so a גט should not be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the deaf-mute is maybe acquired, maybe not, and the minor is partly acquired, then when he has relations with the deaf-mute, why does he give a גט and she is permitted? It is a flawed act, and a flawed act does not exempt her.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רב ששת's proof. He shows that the opposite reading of רב cannot explain the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קטנה is truly, though partly, married to him, the חרשת is in some way his wife's sister. That makes his relations with her a flawed יבום. A flawed יבום does not free her from חליצה, and a חרשת cannot do חליצה. So she should still be stuck, yet the ברייתא says a גט frees her. That only fits רב חסדא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: a flawed (invalid) act of יבום
does not exempt her (from חליצה)
why?

phrases.english: But if you say
the deaf-mute is maybe acquired, maybe not,
and the minor is acquired but not completely,
then when he has relations with the deaf-mute,
why does he give a גט and she is permitted?
It is a flawed act —
phrases.notes: It is flawed because the minor, her sister, is partly married to him.

phrases.english: and a flawed act does not exempt her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by showing that the opposite reading fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opposite reading of רב: the חרשת is a 'maybe' and the קטנה is partly acquired.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, his relations with the חרשת are a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה, which does not exempt her, so the ברייתא's ruling that a גט frees her would not work.

steps.title: The ברייתא may follow רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא could follow רבי נחמיה, who holds that even a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה exempts a woman from חליצה. So the ruling fits the other reading too, and it is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is רבי נחמיה, who said: a flawed act exempts from חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב ששת's proof. It says the ברייתא could follow רבי נחמיה, whose rule makes the problem from step 8 disappear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 8 depended on the rule that a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה does not exempt. רבי נחמיה disagrees and holds that it does exempt. If the ברייתא follows him, the other reading of רב works just as well, so the ברייתא proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: whose opinion is this?
exempts from חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: For now, this pushback weakens רב ששת's proof: the ברייתא might follow רבי נחמיה, who holds that a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה also exempts from חליצה. Steps 10-13 answer this pushback and show the ברייתא follows the רבנן after all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a proof from a ברייתא is rejected by showing that the ברייתא may follow a specific תנא whose view removes the difficulty.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is רבי נחמיה,
who said: a flawed act
exempts from חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 7-8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא for רב חסדא's reading.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה does not exempt, but רבי נחמיה holds that it does, so the ברייתא can fit the other reading too.

steps.title: Quoting the end of the ברייתא against the רבי נחמיה reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה by quoting its last clause. A man married to an orphaned קטנה and an orphaned חרשת died. The יבם had relations with the קטנה and then with the חרשת, or his brother had relations with the חרשת. Both women are now forbidden to him. The fix is that the חרשת leaves with a גט, and the קטנה waits until she grows up and does חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה, look at its last part: a man was married to two orphans, a minor and a deaf-mute, and he died. The יבם had relations with the minor and then with the deaf-mute, or his brother had relations with the deaf-mute. Both women are forbidden to him. How do we fix this? The deaf-mute leaves with a גט, and the minor waits until she grows up and does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to Step 9 by quoting the סֵיפָא, the last clause of the same ברייתא. The next steps will show why this clause does not fit רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 tried to save the flipped reading by saying the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה. Now the גמרא brings a new case from the same ברייתא in which the קטנה must do חליצה. The question will be why she needs חליצה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the last clause of the source
Orphans (girls with no father)
The dead husband's brother, who can do יבום
Both of them became forbidden
How is their situation fixed?

phrases.english: If it is רבי נחמיה,
phrases.notes: This picks up Step 9's claim that the ברייתא might follow רבי נחמיה.

phrases.english: say the last clause:
one who was married to two orphans,
a minor and a deaf-mute, and he died.
The יבם had relations with the minor,
and then had relations with the deaf-mute,
or his brother had relations with the deaf-mute,
both are forbidden to him.
How is their situation fixed?
The deaf-mute leaves with a גט,
and the minor waits until she grows up, and does חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 9's suggestion that the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה by bringing the ברייתא's last clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 9 that the ברייתא may follow רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause requires the קטנה to do חליצה, which needs an explanation that may not work under רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: Why the ruling works under the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the last clause fits well under three assumptions: the חרשת is partly acquired, the קטנה is a 'maybe', and the ברייתא follows the רבנן. חז"ל require the קטנה to do חליצה out of concern that he might have had relations with the חרשת first. In that case his relations with the קטנה would be a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה, and under the רבנן that does not exempt her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well if you say that the deaf-mute is acquired but not fully, that the minor is either acquired or not acquired, and that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. That is why the minor waits until she grows up and does חליצה. Perhaps he went ahead and had relations with the deaf-mute first, and then his relations with the minor would be a flawed act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the last clause fits nicely under the original reading together with the רבנן. This sets up the contrast in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We worry that he might have been with the חרשת first. Then his later relations with the קטנה would be a flawed act. The רבנן hold that a flawed act does not exempt her, so she still needs חליצה once she is grown.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (granted), used before a 'but' challenge
Acquired, but with something lacking (partly married)
Maybe acquired, maybe not (a doubtful marriage)
Because perhaps
First, at the beginning
The majority of the Sages (here, the ones who say a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה does not exempt)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of marriage: the חרשת is 'partly' married (a real but weak marriage), while the קטנה is a 'maybe' (we don't know if she is married at all). Also, the case says he went to the קטנה first. The worry about the חרשת first is a precaution, not what actually happened.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
the deaf-mute is acquired but not fully,
the minor is maybe acquired, maybe not,
and it follows the רבנן,
phrases.notes: These are the רבנן who argue with רבי נחמיה and say a flawed act does not exempt.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי תַּמְתִּין עַד שֶׁתַּגְדִּיל, וְתַחְלוֹץ —

because perhaps he went ahead and had relations with the deaf-mute first,

steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא follows the רבנן, with the חרשת partly acquired and the קטנה a 'maybe'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling in the last clause of the ברייתא that the קטנה must wait and do חליצה

steps.title: Under רבי נחמיה the קטנה would not need חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses the challenge. If the ברייתא followed רבי נחמיה, a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה would exempt the קטנה. Then there would be no reason for her to wait and do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say it follows רבי נחמיה, he said that a flawed act does exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the last clause cannot follow רבי נחמיה, because under his view the קטנה would not need חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason given for the קטנה's חליצה is that her יבום might have been a flawed act. רבי נחמיה says a flawed act still exempts. So under his view the concern disappears, and the ruling makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say
Doesn't he say...? (pointing to a known opinion)
Exempts her (from חליצה)

phrases.english: But if you say it follows רבי נחמיה,
he said a flawed act exempts!
phrases.notes: So under his view the minor's relations would already free her, and she would not need חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה, הָא אָמַר בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה פָּטְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'it works well... but' structure begun in Step 11 by showing the ruling fails under רבי נחמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's suggestion that the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה holds that a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה exempts, so the קטנה would need no חליצה, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: Conclusion: the ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא must follow the רבנן, and it accepts this: 'Learn from it.' This means the original reading stands (the חרשת is partly acquired, and the קטנה is a 'maybe').
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by deciding that the ברייתא follows the רבנן, which undoes the pushback of Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא follows the רבנן, the escape route from Step 9 is closed. So the ברייתא supports the reading that the חרשת is partly acquired and the קטנה is a 'maybe', and the proof from Step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introducing the true conclusion)
Learn from it (the point is proven)
It follows the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the two orphaned sisters follows the רבנן (a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה does not exempt). This shows that a חרשת's marriage is partial, and a קטנה's marriage is a doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the status of the two weak marriages: the חרשת is partly married and the קטנה is a 'maybe'. That is the basis for how the יבום and חליצה rules for these women are decided.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this that it follows the רבנן.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רַבָּנַן הִיא. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the challenge in Step 12 and rejects the pushback of Step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, so the proof stands that a חרשת is partly acquired and a קטנה is a 'maybe'.

steps.title: רב אשי: the first clause also shows the ruling follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues from the רישא. It teaches that if the יבם had relations with the חרשת, he gives her a גט and she is released. It does not teach the same for the קטנה. That implies relations with the קטנה would not free her, which is the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can learn from the first clause too that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. It says that if he had relations with the deaf-mute, he gives her a גט and she is released. It does not say that if he had relations with the minor, he gives her a גט and she is released.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second proof from the first clause that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. His proof is based on something the ברייתא leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא offers the 'relations, then a גט' solution only for the חרשת. רב אשי reads the silence about the קטנה as deliberate. Because the חרשת is partly acquired, relations with the קטנה would be a בִּיאָה פְּסוּלָה. Under the רבנן that would not exempt her, so she would still need חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a teaching

steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's first clause gives the 'relations, then a גט' solution for the חרשת but leaves it out for the קטנה

steps.title: The silence about the minor proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's proof. The חרשת cannot do חליצה, so the only way out for her is a less-than-ideal route: relations and then a גט. The קטנה can wait and do חליצה, which is a proper permitted route, so the ברייתא had no reason to list a forbidden route for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is your reason, it is no proof. The deaf-mute has no permitted way out, so the ברייתא teaches the forbidden way out for her. The minor has a permitted way out, so the ברייתא does not bother teaching a forbidden one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי. It explains another reason why the ברייתא could leave out the 'relations and a גט' route for the קטנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי assumed the ברייתא was silent because that route would fail for the קטנה. The גמרא says the silence can be explained another way. The ברייתא only mentions a forbidden fix when nothing better exists. The קטנה has a better fix, so the silence fits רבי נחמיה just as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a proof; the point does not follow
A permitted way to fix the situation
A fix that uses a forbidden step

steps.whatToRemember: The final proof that the ברייתא follows the רבנן is the one from the סיפא in Step 13. רב אשי's extra proof from the רישא was pushed off.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The silence about the קטנה can be explained because she has a permitted fix. It does not have to mean that relations with her would fail to free her.

steps.title: New משנה: a man married to two orphaned minor girls
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A man was married to two orphaned minor girls and died. The יבם had relations with the first and then with the second, or his brother had relations with the second. The ruling comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man was married to two orphaned minor girls, and he died. The יבם had relations with the first and then had relations with the second. Or his brother had relations with the second.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens and lays out a case. This step is only the setup; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time both wives are minors of the same standing. Neither is more fully married than the other, unlike the earlier case of a קטנה and a חרשת. The case covers two versions: the same יבם goes on to the second wife, or a different brother goes to the second wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Orphaned minor girls (married off by their mother or brothers)
The dead husband's brother, who can do יבום

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. Don't look for the ruling here; it comes in the next part of the משנה.
